sections.html:
Hammond sits in the northwest corner of Indiana on Lake Michigan, inside the Chicago metro area, and it is the only Indiana city that borders Chicago. The 2020 census counted 77,879 residents, down from a peak of 111,698 in 1960. Lake George, Wolf Lake, Oxbow Lake and parts of the Grand Calumet River lie inside the city or along its edge, and much of the ground is former dune and swale on sandy soil.

The South Shore Line stops at Hammond Gateway and South Hammond, and the Borman Expressway and the Indiana Toll Road both run through the area. A house within reach of a station or an expressway ramp has a selling point worth mentioning to any buyer.

Common reasons Hammond owners reach out: a house with water damage, a rental that is more trouble than income, an inherited home shared among relatives and a job change that sets a deadline.

The mills and rail yards drew workers to Hammond for decades, and the city is full of early and mid-twentieth century housing: worker cottages, bungalows and two-flats. Several neighborhoods are historic districts, including Forest-Ivanhoe, Forest-Moraine, Glendale Park, Indi-Illi Park, Pullman-Standard and Roselawn-Forest Heights.

Houses of that age often need electrical, plumbing and foundation work. The price of that work is usually the main reason an owner starts thinking about a cash sale. Get a rough estimate before you decide, so you can see what an as-is price has to cover.

Neighborhood matters too. A cottage in a historic district may need exterior work cleared with the city before anything changes, so ask before you start a project. Buyers in these areas tend to be investors or first-time owners, and each group reads a repair list differently.

Heavy rain has caused sewer backups and wet basements in Hammond. On September 17, 2023, more than four inches fell in seven hours, and the city reported sewer backups in more than 500 homes. Homeowners were urged to install backflow preventers, and the Hammond Sanitary District offered to reimburse up to $2,000 toward the installation. Ask the Sanitary District whether that program is still open.

If your house has taken on water, expect questions from buyers. A financed buyer's inspector and lender will look at the damage, the repairs and the insurance history. A cash buyer prices the same problems but does not wait on an appraisal or a loan approval.

Gather what you have: repair receipts for sump pumps and drainage, any insurance claim history and photos of the basement after a storm. Share them with whoever makes you an offer. Hiding water history tends to backfire when a buyer's inspector finds the stains.

Owners of rental housing in Hammond must register every year, by April 15, under section 96.152 of the city code.

RequirementDetail
New rentalRegister within 30 days of buying the property
Stop renting, sell or transferNotify the Inspections Department within 30 days
Annual fee$5 per unit
Late fee$500 per unit not registered by April 15
InsuranceProof equal to the property's value, or a bond or letter of credit for the greater of the property's value or $25,000
Fines for not registeringUp to $2,500 per unit per day, first violation; $7,500 for later ones

If you own a rental and want to sell, report the sale to the city within the 30 days. Forms and the Code Enforcement office are at City Hall, 5925 Calumet Avenue, phone (219) 853-6300.

Building permits are required for construction and remodeling, and every contractor working in Hammond must be registered with the city. The Building Division is in Room G1 at City Hall, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., phone 219-853-6317.

Plumbing work needs a state plumbing license, and the city lists a minimum plumbing permit fee of $50 that covers the first three fixtures. Heating and cooling contractors take a city exam, and electrical contractors answer to the Electrical Board.

If you plan to renovate before listing, ask the division what applies to your scope. If you sell as-is, there is no renovation to permit.

sections.h2: Property taxes and where to pay
sections.html:
Property tax on a Hammond house goes to the Lake County Treasurer. Offices: Crown Point at 2293 N. Main Street, Hammond at 232 Russell Street (219-933-2900), and Gary.

Each year brings two installments, one in May and one in November (May 11 and November 10 under the 2026 schedule). A payment made up to 30 days late draws a 5 percent penalty, and anything later draws 10 percent.

Back taxes owed at the time of a sale are paid by the title company out of your proceeds at closing. Before you list or accept an offer, call the treasurer's office and ask for your current balance.

Indiana asks for a sales disclosure form with each property transfer. The county assessor sees it first, then the county auditor, all before the deed is filed. A recorder will not record the deed unless proof of the auditor's receipt is attached. This process has been amended before, so have your title company confirm the current steps. The Lake County Recorder shares the Crown Point address with the treasurer.

Wondering whether Hammond demands an inspection before a sale? Phone the Building Division about your address, since rules change.

Listing a Hammond house can mean drying and repairing a basement, updating wiring, bringing a rental into registration and sitting through weeks of showings. A cash sale skips all of it, since we buy houses as-is whatever the repair list looks like.

  1. Tell us about the house, including any water history and tenants.
  2. We make an offer that reflects its condition and location.
  3. If you accept, a title company searches the deed and sets the closing date.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded, and you are paid at closing.

At the first call, have your tax bill, mortgage payoff figures and any lease ready. Weigh the offer against a listing, counting the repairs, the waiting and the monthly costs of holding the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Hammond house if it has flood or sewer damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners sell houses with water damage regularly, but the buyer will want to know the history and the repairs. A cash buyer can take the house as-is and price the repairs itself.

faqs.q: Do I have to report the sale of a Hammond rental to the city?
faqs.a: Yes. An owner who sells or transfers a rental must notify the Inspections Department within 30 days. Annual registration is due April 15, and the late fee is $500 per unit.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments a year, in May and November. A payment within 30 days after the date carries a 5 percent penalty, and later payment carries 10 percent. Pay your county treasurer.

faqs.q: Where do I get a Hammond building permit?
faqs.a: At the Building Division in Room G1 of City Hall, 5925 Calumet Avenue. The phone is 219-853-6317, and the office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Who records the deed in Hammond?
faqs.a: The Lake County Recorder records it, after the county auditor has the Indiana sales disclosure form. Your title or escrow company normally handles both.
